## Design note

The drift scene's favourite: balanced, light, and with a 1.5-way LSD that locks on and off throttle so it holds a slide. Not brutally fast, but the most communicative chassis in the roster and the easiest to throw sideways on purpose.

## How this car breaks

Light coupe shell with long doors and thin sills: side impacts reach the cabin quickly. The front clip is cheap to replace (bumper, hood and fenders bolt on and come off easily). The rear subframe sits right under the boot, so rear-enders bend the axle geometry early.

## Sources (type)

- manufacturer spec-class data for early-2000s 2.0 T FR coupes
- owner dyno averages for 2.0 L turbo I4s in that segment
- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, opposed-piston caliper hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 490 | 0.80 | 390 |
| pitch | 2321 | 0.88 | 2040 |
| yaw | 2453 | 0.88 | 2160 |

## Engine

2.0 L DOHC I4, single ball-bearing turbo, intercooled. Class-typical early-2000s 2.0 T coupe (~92 kW/L); late, flat torque from a larger turbo, per owner dyno averages.

Peak **182 kW @ 6500 rpm**, **276 N·m @ 5000 rpm**. Idle 850 / redline 7200 / limiter 7500 rpm. Rotating inertia 0.13 kg·m² (class: 0.10 small four … 0.30 big-block). Engine braking 12% of peak torque = 33 N·m. Power-to-weight 140 kW/t.

## Drivetrain

6-speed manual, clutch-type 1.5-way rear LSD. Layout **RWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 60 N·m, power ramp 0.45, coast ramp 0.30. Clutch capacity 1.45 × peak torque = 400 N·m. Shift time 0.42 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |

| 1 | 3.32 | 13.55 | 62 |

| 3 | 1.31 | 5.34 | 156 |
| 4 | 1.00 | 4.08 | 205 |
| 5 | 0.76 | 3.10 | 269 |
| 6 | 0.66 | 2.69 | 310 |

Final drive 4.08, reverse 3.38. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.308 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.32 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 338 kg | 1.85 Hz | 45600 N/m | 2510 N·s/m | 3760 N·s/m | 0.13 m |
| Rear | 271 kg | 1.95 Hz | 40600 N/m | 2120 N·s/m | 3180 N·s/m | 0.14 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 2.0°/g with 60% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.362 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 132336 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 49975 F / 43902 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **13400 F / 4200 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 2.0°/g, front share 60%. Bump stops 170000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -1.0° F / -1.3° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 6.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 296 mm disc, pistons per side 42 mm + 42 mm → A = 27.7 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 123 mm, pad μ = 0.42: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.42·100 bar·27.7 cm²·0.123 m = **2863 N·m**
- Rear: 297 mm disc, pistons per side 38 mm → A = 11.3 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 124 mm, pad μ = 0.4: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.4·100 bar·11.3 cm²·0.123 m = **1121 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 2863 / 1121 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.20), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.89 → **2550 / 1000 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1417 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.80×), rear needs 526 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.90×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 946 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.514** → delivered 2550 N·m front / 946 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1330 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 15.0:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 9.3 m → outer-front path radius 4.54 m, rear-axle-centre radius 3.04 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.694 rad (39.7°)** (outer 33.8°, inner 47.7° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.50). Rack speed 1.6 rad/s.
